p01.why: tl is built either before main or at first use; both cases leave before as 0 or 4 and trace as 4 after the read, so main returns 0.

p02.why: Whether tl is built before main or at its first use, it is built by the time tl.id is read, so trace is 4 and main returns 0.

p03.why: The new object is never deleted, so its destructor never runs and trace stays 1.

p04.why: Constant evaluation destroys b before a, so tr becomes 2 then 21 and the static_assert holds; there is no main, so the program is not run.

p05.why: Members a and b are built (1, 2), then the ~W body runs (9), then the members end in reverse (2, 1), giving 12921.

p06.why: The temporary bound to r lives until the block ends, so the order is 1, 2, 1, 3, giving 1213.

p07.why: Distinct complete objects and distinct array elements have different addresses, and an empty class has size 1.

p08.why: Reading *p after delete is undefined, and constant evaluation rejects it.

p09.why: The reference to x does not extend x, so reading through keep after the block ends is undefined and constant evaluation rejects it.

p11.why: x ends with its block, and the read through p is undefined, so constant evaluation rejects it.

p12.why: Array elements are built first to last and destroyed last to first, giving 123321.

p13.why: Writing u.f reuses the storage of u.i and ends its lifetime, so reading r is undefined and constant evaluation rejects it.

p14.why: The inner block ends b before c begins, giving 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 1, which is 122331.

p15.why: x is written before it is read, so the read is valid and gives 4.

p16.why: The function-local static is built at the first call only, giving 1, 5, 2; its destruction after main does not change the exit status.

p17.why: The dynamic object outlives make and ends only at delete, giving 1, 2, 3, 1.

p18.why: The return destroys b then a, and mark(9) is never reached, giving 1221.

p19.why: x has no value when it is read, which is undefined, and constant evaluation rejects it.

p20.why: The temporary ends after use returns and before mark(2), giving 1, 5, 1, 2.

p21.why: never is never called, so its static object is never built and trace stays 0.

p22.why: Each iteration builds and destroys its own a, giving 1, 1, 2, 2.

p23.why: Reading x through p after its block ends is undefined, and constant evaluation rejects it.

p24.why: No initializer gives p.y a value, so reading it is undefined and constant evaluation rejects it.

p25.why: a and b are built before seen is initialized and before the body runs, so seen is 12 and trace ends as 123.

p26.why: The address of x does not change during its lifetime, so p equals q and *p is 5.

p27.why: first and second are built before main (12), local adds 3 and 3, then statics end in reverse (2, 1), so Last, built first and ended last, sees 123321 and does not write through null.
